question: A lattice point is a point in the plane with integer coordinates. How many lattice points are on the line segment whose endpoints are \((3,17)\) and \((48,281)?\) (Include both endpoints of the segment in your count.)
solution:
For a lattice point, both coordinate changes from \((3,17)\) must be integers. The segment has slope
\[
\frac{281-17}{48-3}=\frac{264}{45}=\frac{88}{15}.
\]
Thus a point \((x,y)\) on it satisfies
\[
y-17=\frac{88}{15}(x-3),\qquad 3\le x\le48.
\]
Since \(88\) and \(15\) have no common factor greater than \(1\), an integer \(x-3\) makes the right side an integer exactly when \(x-3\) is a multiple of \(15\).

The allowed horizontal displacements are therefore \(0,15,30,45\), producing
\[
(3,17),\ (18,105),\ (33,193),\ (48,281).
\]
Each lies on the segment, and every lattice point on the segment has one of these displacements. Their distinct horizontal coordinates prevent double counting. Including both endpoints, there are \(\boxed{4}\) lattice points, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

edges.reason: Perpendicular constructions and uniqueness explain orthogonal projections, but plotting on an existing square grid needs only its given axes. Keep the useful geometry preparation without imposing the full construction workflow.
Each coordinate axis is a number line with an origin, a direction and a unit. Plotting and reading coordinates is impossible without understanding those three elements of a number line.
edges.scope: coordinate axes as two perpendicular number lines

edges.reason: Each axis is a signed number line, so plotting signed coordinates uses number-to-position interpretation on it.
edges.scope: axes as number lines with negatives

edges.reason: A point's two coordinates form an ordered pair; swapping the entries generally changes the point.

The criteria expressly find common factors and reduce until numerator and denominator are coprime. These are the common-factor contents of the endpoint; finding the greatest factor in a single step is only a shortcut and is outside this required scope.
edges.scope: Finding a shared divisor and recognizing the absence of a shared divisor above one when reducing to simplest form

edges.reason: Reduction replaces numerator and denominator by division by the same common factor, using the value-preserving fraction property.
edges.scope: dividing numerator and denominator by a common number

edges.reason: The gcd(|dx|,|dy|)+1 formula is the efficient route for segments. Region counts use column-wise bounds, and small segments can be handled by parametrizing and checking integrality.
edges.scope: gcd formula for lattice points on a segment

edges.reason: Lattice points are defined by coordinates, and regions are translated into coordinate inequalities. Reading and plotting coordinates in a Cartesian plane is therefore unavoidable.
